sources.entry: Atticus - Open-source voice assistant that runs on your Claude plan, learns new tasks after doing them once, and handles dictation, screen help, and background agents. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/SaarthurR/atticus-mac) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Atticus
summary.one_liner: Atticus is a free, open-source voice assistant for macOS that runs on your Claude Pro or Max plan and controls apps, windows, and the screen through speech.
use_cases: Open apps and move windows by voice
Dictate and reply to messages or emails
Get answers about a call while it is happening
Run multi-step research tasks in a background agent
Automate repetitive Mac actions after teaching them once
summary.what_it_does: Atticus is a voice assistant for macOS that is activated with a keyboard shortcut (Control+Option+Space on the page). It can open apps, move windows, find files, search the web, click buttons, type replies, and play music. Speech is converted to text on the Mac, and the page says audio never leaves the Mac. Big jobs run in a background agent that shows a live mini screen and can be steered from a text box. Users can say "remember" to teach it preferences, and tasks it has learned are then handled without AI calls. The page says it uses the user's existing Claude Pro or Max plan rather than an API key.
notable: Runs on existing Claude Pro or Max plan with no API key
Learns tasks after one run; repeated tasks skip the AI and run for free
Background agents with a live mini screen, and screen-aware help that points at UI elements
caveats: Requires a Claude Pro or Max subscription
Misheard words are handled by safety guards, but the page does not detail them
